summary.title: Testing Distributed Systems
summary.one_liner: A curated reading list of papers, talks, tools and company case studies on how distributed systems are tested, from Jepsen and formal methods to deterministic simulation, autonomous testing, fuzzing and chaos engineering.
keywords: how do companies test distributed databases
takeaways: Jepsen and Elle are the main black-box approaches for checking consistency and isolation anomalies in databases and distributed systems.
Deterministic simulation (pioneered by FoundationDB) and autonomous testing (Antithesis) are presented as leading approaches for finding bugs in distributed systems.
Formal methods such as TLA+ are used by AWS, Microsoft, MongoDB, Elastic, CockroachDB and others to verify algorithm designs.
The list includes company-specific testing practices from AWS, Netflix, Google, Meta, Cassandra and ScyllaDB, with links to talks and papers.
summary.summary: This is a curated link list by Andrey Satarin covering how distributed systems are tested. It is organized by approach (Jepsen, formal methods/TLA+, deterministic simulation, autonomous testing, fuzzing, chaos engineering, performance benchmarking, test case reduction) and by company or system (AWS, Netflix, Microsoft, Meta, FoundationDB, Cassandra, ScyllaDB and others). Each entry is a one-line description pointing to papers, talks, blog posts or tools, and it also includes studies of real bugs and failures in cloud systems.
